subject: Geopolitics
title: Oil and the Middle East
description: A short lesson to help you apply Oil and the Middle East.

hook.text: Would the West care about the Persian Gulf if it grew wheat instead of pumping oil? Strategic interest follows energy.

buildup.text: Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, and the UAE sit atop the world's richest oil fields. Wars have been fought over each.

discovery.text: Oil revenue built gleaming cities but also funded authoritarian regimes. Wealth without accountability is the pattern.

twist.text: The 1973 Arab oil embargo showed producers could weaponize supply. Prices quadrupled and the West panicked.

climax.text: Oil made the Middle East strategically vital and politically turbulent. The resource shapes both power and instability.

punchline.text: Oil built the kingdom. Oil also keeps it fragile.

quiz.question: What did the 1973 Arab oil embargo demonstrate?
options: Oil consumers could always find alternatives quickly
Oil producers could weaponize supply to cause economic pain
The Middle East had no influence over global markets
